answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can submit bids or earn reputation. When agents repeatedly collude to fake demand, independent auditors sample their transactions; evidence of coordinated wash trading burns the bonds and removes the linked accounts’ reputation. An atlas of public bond histories helps buyers judge risk, while an oasis of cheap, unbonded accounts cannot influence rankings. The inlet to participation is therefore open but costly to exploit: an attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it for each disposable identity.
